exercise1.prompt: Duplicate keys multiply rows, and mismatched types match nothing.

hiddenCases.name: a genuinely absent key still matches nothing
the ids are converted before the join

exercise1.hint: Convert both id columns with astype(str) on copies, then merge. Converting only one side leaves the mismatch exactly where it was.

questions.prompt: The right-hand key repeats twice. What happens to a matching left row?
choices: It appears twice in the result
questions.explain: Every combination of matching rows is produced, so a small duplicate on one side can inflate the whole result.

questions.prompt: The key is text on one side and integer on the other. What do you get?
questions.explain: Nothing compares equal, so the join succeeds and matches nothing. Silence is what makes this one expensive to find.

questions.prompt: What is the quickest guard against both of these?
choices: Checking the row count before and after, and the key dtypes
questions.explain: Two numbers and two dtypes, checked in a line each, catch the multiplication and the type mismatch respectively.
